your backend. If you chose to have your backend as a library (seem the
backends/bmv2 example), the library should depend on `genIR`, and
there is no longer necessary for your executable to depend on it.

```
add_executable(p4c-mybackend ${MY_SOURCES})
target_link_libraries (p4c-mybackend ${P4C_LIBRARIES} ${P4C_LIB_DEPS})
add_dependencies(p4c-mybackend genIR)
```

### Tests

We implemented support equivalent to the automake `make check` rules.
All tests should be included in `make check` and in addition, we support
`make check-*` rules. To enable this support, add the following rules:

```
set(MY_DRIVER <driver or compiler executable>)

set (MY_TEST_SUITES
  ${P4C_SOURCE_DIR}/testdata/p4_16_samples/*.p4
  ${P4C_SOURCE_DIR}/testdata/p4_16_errors/*.p4
  )
set (MY_XFAIL_TESTS
  testdata/p4_16_errors/this_test_fails.p4
 )
p4c_add_tests("mybackend" ${MY_DRIVER} "${MY_TEST_SUITES}" "${MY_XFAIL_TESTS}")
```

In addition, you can add individual tests to a suite using the following macro:
```
set(isXFail FALSE)
set(SWITCH_P4 testdata/p4_14_samples/switch_20160512/switch.p4)

p4c_add_test_with_args ("mybackend" ${MY_DRIVER} ${isXFail}
  "switch_with_custom_profile" ${SWITCH_P4} "-DCUSTOM_PROFILE")
```

See the documentation for
[`p4c_add_test_with_args`](cmake/P4CUtils.cmake) and
[`p4c_add_tests`](cmake/P4CUtils.cmake) for more information on the
arguments to these macros.

To pass custom arguments to p4c, you can set the environment variable `P4C_ARGS`:
```
make check P4C_ARGS="-Xp4c=MY_CUSTOM_FLAG"
```

### Installation

Define rules to install your backend. Typically you need to install
the binary, the additional architecture headers, and the configuration
file for the p4c driver.

```
install (TARGETS p4c-mybackend
  RUNTIME DESTINATION ${P4C_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY})
install (DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/p4include
  DESTINATION ${P4C_ARTIFACTS_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY})
install (FILES ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/driver/p4c.mybackend.cfg
  DESTINATION ${P4C_ARTIFACTS_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY}/p4c_src)
```

# Known issues

The P4C compiler is in early development. Issues with the compiler are
tracked on [GitHub](https://github.com/p4lang/p4c/issues). Before
opening a new issue, please check whether a similar issue is already
opened. Opening issues and submitting a pull request with fixes for
those issues is much appreciated.

In addition to the list of issues on Github, there are a number of
currently unsupported features listed below:

## Frontend

### P4_14 features not supported in P4_16

* extern/blackbox attributes -- there is support for carrying them in
the IR, but they are lost if P4_16 code is output.  Backends can
access them from the IR

* Nonstandard extension primitives from P4_14
  * Execute_meter extra arguments
  * Recirculate variants
  * Bypass_egress
  * Sample_ primitives
  * invalidate

* No support for P4_14 parser exceptions.

## Backends

### Bmv2 Backend

* Range "set" not supported in parser transitions
* Tables with multiple apply calls

See also [unsupported P4_16 language features](backends/bmv2/README.md#unsupported-p4_16-language-features).
annotation: Parses and validates a custom header sequence with variable number of h2 headers, recording validity in h1 header.
detailed_annotation: Parses a sequence of headers (h1, h2, h3) with specific validation rules for each header type.
Handles a variable number of h2 headers (up to MAX_H2_HEADERS) and records their validity in the h1 header.
Employs a sub-parser to handle the parsing of h2 headers.
Verifies header types and transitions between parsing states based on the next header type field.
Deparses the headers in the correct order (h1, h2, h3) for output.

# Petr4
The Petr4 project is developing the formal semantics of the [P4
Language](https://p4.org) backed by an independent reference implementation.

# POPL'21 artifact
See https://verified-network-toolchain.github.io/petr4/ or check out the `gh-pages` branch
for information on the Petr4 artifact.

# Getting Started

## Installing Petr4

1. Install OPAM 2 following the official [OPAM installation
   instructions](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html). Make sure `opam
   --version` reports version 2 or later.

1. Install external dependencies:
   ```
   sudo apt-get install m4 libgmp-dev
   ```

### Installing from OPAM
1. Install petr4 from the opam repository. This will take a while the first time
   because it installs OPAM dependencies.
   ```
   opam install petr4
   ```

### Installing from source
You can use the [scripts](https://github.com/verified-network-toolchain/petr4/tree/main/.github/scripts) to install Petr4. 
Alternatively, follow theses steps:
1. Check the installed version of OCaml:
    ```
    ocamlc -v
    ```
    If the version is less than 4.09.1, upgrade:
    ```
    opam switch 4.09.1
    ```

1. Install [p4pp](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/p4pp) from source.
1. Install Coq and Bignum.
   ```
   opam install coq
   opam install bignum
   ```
   If this doesn't work, install the dependencies manually.
   ```
   opam install ANSITerminal alcotest bignum cstruct-sexp pp ppx_deriving ppx_import ppx_deriving_yojson yojson js_of_ocaml js_of_ocaml-lwt js_of_ocaml-ppx
   ```

1. Build bundled dependencies.
   ```
   opam repo add coq-released https://coq.inria.fr/opam/released
   opam pin add coq-vst-zlist https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/VST.git
   ```

1. Use dune to build and install petr4.
   ```
   opam install . --deps-only
   opam exec -- dune build
   dune install
   ```

1. [Optional] Run tests
   ``` 
   make test
   ```

   To run the CI tests locally:
   ```
   opam exec -- make ci-test
   ```

   To run STF tests:
   ```
   opam exec -- make test-stf
   ```


## Running Petr4

Currently `petr4` is merely a P4 front-end. By default, it will parse
a source program to an abstract syntax tree and print it out, either
as P4 or encoded into JSON.

Run `petr4 -help` to see the list of currently-supported options.

## Web user interface

`petr4` uses `js_of_ocaml` to provide a web interface. To compile to javascript,
run `make web`. Then open `index.html` in `html_build` in a browser.


# Contributing

Petr4 is an open-source project. We encourage contributions!
Please file issues on
[Github](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/petr4/issues).

# Credits

See the list of [contributors](CONTRIBUTORS).

# License

Petr4 is released under the [Apache2 License](LICENSE).
annotation: Drops all incoming packets
detailed_annotation: The `MyIngress` control block is where the main logic resides, and it marks all packets to be dropped using `mark_to_drop`.
The parser `MyParser` immediately transitions to the `accept` state, indicating that it doesn't parse any headers.
The `MyChecksum` and `MyDeparser` control blocks are empty, implying that no checksum computation or packet serialization is performed.
The `MyEgress` control block is also empty, meaning no processing is done on packets after they are routed.

annotation: Parses Ethernet packets with various etherTypes, extracts corresponding headers, and modifies the Ethernet destination address based on header validity.
detailed_annotation: The parser uses a `select` statement on the Ethernet `etherType` to determine which header to extract next.
The program extracts one of five possible headers (`h0` to `h4`) based on specific `etherType` values or ranges.
In the ingress control, the program modifies specific bits of the Ethernet `dstAddr` based on the validity of the extracted headers.
The program sets the `egress_spec` to a fixed value (3) for all packets.
The Deparser emits the Ethernet header followed by any valid headers that were extracted during parsing.

annotation: Program implements a simple forwarding decision based on a register value.
detailed_annotation: Uses a register to store a single bit value that is read and used to determine forwarding behavior.
The register value is cast to a boolean metadata field (`meta.test`) to control the forwarding decision.
An exact match table (`debug_table`) is used to apply either a `drop` or `forward` action based on the value of `meta.test`.

The program does not perform any header parsing or modification.

annotation: Perform exact match lookup on a metadata field and execute an action with a predefined value.
detailed_annotation: The program uses a metadata field `test` as the key for an exact match table `test_table`.
The `test_table` has a constant entry that maps the value `1` to the action `act` with parameter `1`.
The `IngressImpl` control block applies the `test_table` to perform the lookup and execute the action.
The program uses the V1Model architecture, which is a standard model for P4 programs.
The `act` action takes a `test_t` parameter, which is a typedef for `bit<8>`.

1. Install OPAM 2 following the official [OPAM installation
   instructions](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html). Make sure `opam
   --version` reports version 2 or later.

1. Install external dependencies:
   ```
   sudo apt-get install m4 libgmp-dev
   ```

### Installing from OPAM
1. Install petr4 from the opam repository. This will take a while the first time
   because it installs OPAM dependencies.
   ```
   opam install petr4
   ```

### Installing from source
You can use the [scripts](https://github.com/verified-network-toolchain/petr4/tree/main/.github/scripts) to install Petr4. 
Alternatively, follow theses steps:
1. Check the installed version of OCaml:
    ```
    ocamlc -v
    ```
    If the version is less than 4.09.1, upgrade:
    ```
    opam switch 4.09.1
    ```

1. Install [p4pp](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/p4pp) from source.
1. Install Coq and Bignum.
   ```
   opam install coq
   opam install bignum
   ```
   If this doesn't work, install the dependencies manually.
   ```
   opam install ANSITerminal alcotest bignum cstruct-sexp pp ppx_deriving ppx_import ppx_deriving_yojson yojson js_of_ocaml js_of_ocaml-lwt js_of_ocaml-ppx
   ```

1. Build bundled dependencies.
   ```
   opam repo add coq-released https://coq.inria.fr/opam/released
   opam pin add coq-vst-zlist https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/VST.git
   ```

1. Use dune to build and install petr4.
   ```
   opam install . --deps-only
   opam exec -- dune build
   dune install
   ```

1. [Optional] Run tests
   ``` 
   make test
   ```

   To run the CI tests locally:
   ```
   opam exec -- make ci-test
   ```

   To run STF tests:
   ```
   opam exec -- make test-stf
   ```


## Running Petr4

Currently `petr4` is merely a P4 front-end. By default, it will parse
a source program to an abstract syntax tree and print it out, either
as P4 or encoded into JSON.

Run `petr4 -help` to see the list of currently-supported options.

## Web user interface

`petr4` uses `js_of_ocaml` to provide a web interface. To compile to javascript,
run `make web`. Then open `index.html` in `html_build` in a browser.


# Contributing

Petr4 is an open-source project. We encourage contributions!
Please file issues on
[Github](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/petr4/issues).

# Credits

See the list of [contributors](CONTRIBUTORS).

# License

Petr4 is released under the [Apache2 License](LICENSE).

annotation: Program parses packets, matches against a value set, and performs exact matching on metadata in a table.
detailed_annotation: The parser extracts a `data_h` header and transitions to different states based on a value set match using specific bits of the header fields.
The value set is defined with a custom struct type `value_set_t` containing bit fields of different widths.
The `MyIngress` control block applies a table that performs exact matching on a field within the `my_metadata` struct.
The program uses a V1Switch architecture with various control blocks, although some (like checksum computation and deparsing) are empty or no-ops.
The parser has multiple states, including a `foo` state that simply accepts the packet.

annotation: Parses packets based on complex ternary, LPM, exact, and range matches, and applies an exact-match table in the ingress pipeline.
detailed_annotation: The parser uses a value_set with ternary, LPM, exact, and range matches to determine the parsing path.
The parser extracts a `data_h` header and performs a table lookup based on specific bit fields within the header.
The ingress pipeline applies an exact-match table `t` using a key derived from the `meta.data[0].da` field.
The program uses a custom metadata structure `my_metadata` with an array of `data_h` headers.
The parser transitions to different states based on the match results, with one of the states (`foo`) simply accepting the packet.

annotation: Route packets based on a custom header's fields using a table with optional key matching
detailed_annotation: The program parses a custom header with fields `e`, `t`, `l`, `r`, and `v`.
The `ingress` control uses a table `t_optional` with optional key matching on fields `e` and `t` of the custom header.
The table `t_optional` has multiple entries with different combinations of exact and wildcard matches, influencing the egress port.
The default action is taken when no other entry matches, demonstrating a fallback behavior.
Actions `a` and `a_with_control_params` are used to set the egress port based on the table match results.

annotation: Implements a fabric switch pipeline with various features like packet filtering, forwarding, and INT (In-band Network Telemetry).

Packet IO handling for packet-in and packet-out messages to/from the controller.

# Petr4
The Petr4 project is developing the formal semantics of the [P4
Language](https://p4.org) backed by an independent reference implementation.

# POPL'21 artifact
See https://verified-network-toolchain.github.io/petr4/ or check out the `gh-pages` branch
for information on the Petr4 artifact.

# Getting Started

## Installing Petr4

1. Install OPAM 2 following the official [OPAM installation
   instructions](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html). Make sure `opam
   --version` reports version 2 or later.

1. Install external dependencies:
   ```
   sudo apt-get install m4 libgmp-dev
   ```

### Installing from OPAM
1. Install petr4 from the opam repository. This will take a while the first time
   because it installs OPAM dependencies.
   ```
   opam install petr4
   ```

### Installing from source
You can use the [scripts](https://github.com/verified-network-toolchain/petr4/tree/main/.github/scripts) to install Petr4. 
Alternatively, follow theses steps:
1. Check the installed version of OCaml:
    ```
    ocamlc -v
    ```
    If the version is less than 4.09.1, upgrade:
    ```
    opam switch 4.09.1
    ```

1. Install [p4pp](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/p4pp) from source.
1. Install Coq and Bignum.
   ```
   opam install coq
   opam install bignum
   ```
   If this doesn't work, install the dependencies manually.
   ```
   opam install ANSITerminal alcotest bignum cstruct-sexp pp ppx_deriving ppx_import ppx_deriving_yojson yojson js_of_ocaml js_of_ocaml-lwt js_of_ocaml-ppx
   ```

1. Build bundled dependencies.
   ```
   opam repo add coq-released https://coq.inria.fr/opam/released
   opam pin add coq-vst-zlist https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/VST.git
   ```

1. Use dune to build and install petr4.
   ```
   opam install . --deps-only
   opam exec -- dune build
   dune install
   ```

1. [Optional] Run tests
   ``` 
   make test
   ```

   To run the CI tests locally:
   ```
   opam exec -- make ci-test
   ```

   To run STF tests:
   ```
   opam exec -- make test-stf
   ```


## Running Petr4

Currently `petr4` is merely a P4 front-end. By default, it will parse
a source program to an abstract syntax tree and print it out, either
as P4 or encoded into JSON.

Run `petr4 -help` to see the list of currently-supported options.

## Web user interface

`petr4` uses `js_of_ocaml` to provide a web interface. To compile to javascript,
run `make web`. Then open `index.html` in `html_build` in a browser.

Petr4 is an open-source project. We encourage contributions!

[Github](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/petr4/issues).

# Credits

See the list of [contributors](CONTRIBUTORS).

# License

detailed_annotation: The parser extracts headers from the packet and performs state transitions based on the extracted header values.

## Installing Petr4

1. Install OPAM 2 following the official [OPAM installation
   instructions](https://opam.ocaml.org/doc/Install.html). Make sure `opam
   --version` reports version 2 or later.

1. Install external dependencies:
   ```
   sudo apt-get install m4 libgmp-dev
   ```

### Installing from OPAM
1. Install petr4 from the opam repository. This will take a while the first time
   because it installs OPAM dependencies.
   ```
   opam install petr4
   ```

### Installing from source
You can use the [scripts](https://github.com/verified-network-toolchain/petr4/tree/main/.github/scripts) to install Petr4. 
Alternatively, follow theses steps:
1. Check the installed version of OCaml:
    ```
    ocamlc -v
    ```
    If the version is less than 4.09.1, upgrade:
    ```
    opam switch 4.09.1
    ```

1. Install [p4pp](https://github.com/cornell-netlab/p4pp) from source.
1. Install Coq and Bignum.
   ```
   opam install coq
   opam install bignum
   ```
   If this doesn't work, install the dependencies manually.
   ```
   opam install ANSITerminal alcotest bignum cstruct-sexp pp ppx_deriving ppx_import ppx_deriving_yojson yojson js_of_ocaml js_of_ocaml-lwt js_of_ocaml-ppx
   ```

1. Build bundled dependencies.
   ```
   opam repo add coq-released https://coq.inria.fr/opam/released
   opam pin add coq-vst-zlist https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/VST.git
   ```

1. Use dune to build and install petr4.
   ```
   opam install . --deps-only
   opam exec -- dune build
   dune install
   ```

1. [Optional] Run tests
   ``` 
   make test
   ```

   To run the CI tests locally:
   ```
   opam exec -- make ci-test
   ```

   opam exec -- make test-stf

annotation: Program swaps and modifies specific elements in a 10-element array header during ingress processing.
detailed_annotation: The parser extracts 6 elements from the array header.
The `MyIngress` control plane increments indices and swaps elements in the array header, applying a specific modification function `f` to the elements.
The `f` function sets the values of two input elements to specific constants (0xAA and 0xBB).
The `incr` function is used to increment the index when accessing the array elements.
The modified array header is then emitted by the deparser.
